5. Mr. Md. Afsar Uddin Khan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of petitioner has submitted that as per amended provision of section 96 of the SA&T Act a pre-emptor has to deposit the consideration money together with 25% compensation, and he is also require to pay 8% simple annual interest upon the consideration money from the date of execution of the deed to till filing of the application for pre-emption and that if the case is not filed just after his knowledge about the transfer, the interest will be increased heavily in case of a big amount of consideration money like the present one. He further has submitted that the learned Judge most illegally held that to fill up the lacuna, the petitioner has filed the said application for stay but how the lacuna will be filled up if the proceeding of the case is stayed for a limited period that has not been clearly stated. He also has submitted that if the proceeding of the miscellaneous case is not stayed till completion of registration of the impugned deed, under section 60 of the Registration Act the preemption cage will be dismissed on the ground of maintainability and as such the application for stay of further proceeding of the miscellaneous case is required to be allowed. 

 9. Already the petitioner has paid Tk. one lac as 8% interest for one year along with the application for preemption. Before amendment of Section 96 of the S9ka&T. Act, there was provision for bringing the application for pre-emption after registration of the deed under section 60 of the Registration Act together with 10% compensation but after amendment that provision has been omitted. In such circumstance, the case reported in 34 DLR (AD) 220 cited by the learned Advocate for the opposite party that before registration of the transfer deed under section 60 of the Registration Act the application for preemption is not maintainable, is not applicable in case of those cases which are filed after amendment of Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The law cannot compel a person who comes before the Court for establishing his statutory right to bring the said application with compensatory interest as provided by section 96(3)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and that is also not the intention of the legislature. So, we accept the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that it is not expected that the registration of the impugned deed under section 60 of the Registration Act will be completed within next 4/5 years when the learned Advocate for the other side does not deny the said submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
